summary: Pin migration blocked by edge authz header rewrite during optional canary opt-in
description:
Issue summary: Customer NimbusChat reported that after opting a subset of tenants into a scheduled canary, some sessions that were explicitly pinned to the new model variant were unexpectedly routed to the fallback (legacy) variant.
Impact: Several customer tenants experienced degraded quality and a small cost spike due to re-evaluation on the legacy variant. Scope appears limited to a subset of tenants on us-east who use the customer's SSO flow.
Environment: Production (dedicated pool) - us-east.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer enables canary opt-in via console for a tenant and pins that tenant to redwood-v1.3.
2) Tenant opens a session in their app (long-running streaming session).
3) After a short time (10-30s), requests for that session are observed hitting the legacy variant and receiving degraded responses.
Observed behavior:
- Pin metadata initially applied (control-plane snapshot shows pinned=redwood-v1.3)
- Edge logs show requests arriving without the tenant claim header intermittently
- Orchestrator reports "no pin found" and route falls back to legacy-variant
- No GPU preempt events or autoscaler activity coincide with the times.
Recent change/context: Customer recently enabled an A/B header rewrite rule at their edge proxy to remove trailing user attributes for GDPR compliance. That rule was deployed at the same time as the canary opt-in.
Temporary workaround: Customer disabled the header rewrite rule at their edge which immediately restored pinned routing.
Support notes: We believe an authz/header rewrite at the customer's edge is stripping or renaming the tenant-claim header used in our pin handshake, which prevents the orchestrator from binding the session to the pinned model.
